ADA Business Solutions: what it is, what it runs on, and the alternatives

Review for Surge, 11 November 2026. Everything here is from public pages and public DNS records; nothing was logged into.

The short version. ADA's app (app.adabusinesssol.com) is GoHighLevel with ADA's name and logo on it. GoHighLevel is a large CRM and marketing platform that lets agencies resell it under their own brand, which is a normal, allowed arrangement. ADA itself is a small agency (1 to 10 people) in Effort, Pennsylvania. What Surge pays ADA for is the setup, the support and a markup on top of GoHighLevel.

The same software can be bought directly from GoHighLevel from $97 a month, plus usage charges for texts, calls, email and AI. Whether that is cheaper depends on what Surge pays ADA today, which this review does not have.

Update, 11 Nov: what is inside Surge's account

Matthew logged in and took screenshots (Cai's login, which is an Account admin). Surge pays ADA $500 a week, about $2,170 a month or $26,000 a year.

What this means for the $500 a week. The visible setup was built in April 2026 and has barely changed since. The software itself, bought direct, is $97 to $297 a month, and at Surge's volume (about 1,000 texts and a few hundred emails a month) the usage charges are small next to the fee. The ads in the report are not Surge's, so unless ADA runs recruiting ads for Surge from its own ad account, Surge is paying about $2,000 a month mostly for upkeep of automations it cannot see, and going direct would save most of it.

Many of the Charity Pipeline leads are marked as coming from Facebook. Where those come from (organic job posts, a lead form on Surge's page, or ads ADA runs on Surge's page from another account) is the one thing to settle before deciding.

Questions this raises:

  • Is any ad running on Surge's Facebook page from an account other than Surge's? Meta's public Ad Library shows every ad running under the page, whoever pays for it. Also check which businesses have access to the page.
  • Why is another business's ad account connected to Surge's account? If other clients' ad data shows in Surge's account, ask ADA how Surge's candidate data is kept apart from other clients'.
  • Does Surge own surgeftwtx.com? Candidate emails from two logins depend on it.
  • Will ADA share a snapshot of the workflows if Surge moves? Without it the automations have to be rebuilt by hand.

1. Is it a skinned version of another company? Yes: GoHighLevel

Three separate things point to GoHighLevel:

  1. The app's address points to GoHighLevel. app.adabusinesssol.com is a DNS alias for whitelabel.ludicrous.cloud. GoHighLevel's own help article tells agencies to point their branded app address at exactly that name.
  2. The login page loads GoHighLevel's files. The page's code pulls its files from leadconnectorhq.com, GoHighLevel's platform (LeadConnector is GoHighLevel's company name for the software).
  3. The feature list matches GoHighLevel's. ADA's pricing page lists Missed Call Text Back, AI SMS Conversations, AI Web Chat, Automated Review Requests, Call Recording & Transcripts, Multi-Location Management and similar. These are GoHighLevel's standard features, under GoHighLevel's own names.

Surge is already connected to it. Surge's own address hr.surgeftw.com is set up to send email through LeadConnector (GoHighLevel) and Mailgun, the mail service GoHighLevel uses. So candidate emails already go out as Surge from this GoHighLevel account.

"ADA AI" is most likely GoHighLevel's built-in AI (its "AI Employee": AI replies to texts and web chat, AI booking, call summaries), set up and worded by ADA. That can't be confirmed from outside the account.

2. Who ADA is

  • Location: Effort, Pennsylvania (their privacy policy names "ADA Business Solutions, Effort, PA"; Glassdoor lists the same).
  • Size: 1 to 10 employees (job-board listing). Public contact: Hannah Roybal.
  • What they sell: the branded CRM (GoHighLevel), AI setup, Meta / Google / LinkedIn ads including recruiting ads, and WordPress websites. They describe themselves as women-owned and operated.
  • Their website: WordPress, built from a bought design template (Envato). The site has been up since at least May 2022 and most pages were rebuilt in July 2026.

Worth knowing before trusting the website's claims:

  • The pricing page shows "Starting at $0 / Month" on all three plans: real prices are not published.
  • The homepage says "Trusted by 5,000+ teams worldwide", and the About page shows a four-person team (Founder & CEO, CTO, Product Designer, Head of Growth) with photos named founder-1.png to founder-5.png. These read like text and photos left over from the design template; the only named contact found in public listings is Hannah Roybal. Not proven either way, but worth asking who actually works on Surge's account.

3. What the same software costs direct

GoHighLevel's published prices (gohighlevel.com/pricing, checked 11 Nov 2026):

PlanPriceWhat it is for
Starter$97 / month
$970 / year		One business using the CRM, calendar, email and text automations, pipelines. This covers what Surge uses ADA for.
Unlimited$297 / month
$2,970 / year		Unlimited accounts; for agencies running many clients.
Agency Pro$497 / month
$4,970 / year		Reselling under your own brand. This is the plan ADA is on (or above).

On top of any plan: usage for texts, phone calls, email sending and the AI features is billed separately. That is true whether Surge pays GoHighLevel or ADA.

4. The three options

OptionMonthly costUpsideDownside
Stay with ADAWhatever ADA charges nowSomeone else sets up and maintains the automations, AI and ads. Nothing changes for the team.Paying a markup. If ADA holds the account, ADA holds Surge's candidate data.
Go direct to GoHighLevelFrom $97 + usageSame software, likely much cheaper. Surge owns the account and the data.Someone at Surge has to build and look after the workflows, calendars and AI. The move from ADA's account needs ADA's cooperation (a transfer, or exporting contacts and rebuilding).

GoHighLevel at $97 already does all of this.

5. Recommendation

  1. Get the numbers first. What does Surge pay ADA each month, what is in the contract (term, cancellation notice), and who owns the GoHighLevel account and the candidate data?
  2. Compare against $97 to $297 a month plus usage. If ADA charges several hundred dollars a month or more and mostly keeps things running, going direct is likely the cheaper path. If ADA also runs Surge's recruiting ads and builds the workflows, part of that fee is real work that would have to be replaced.
  3. Building our own is not worth it for Surge alone. It only makes sense if Surge needs something GoHighLevel cannot do. It would be a project in its own right, not a cost saving.

Questions for ADA (or whoever holds the contract)

  • Is the account on your agency's GoHighLevel, and can it be transferred to Surge's own GoHighLevel account if Surge moves?
  • What exactly is "ADA AI" built on, and what does Surge pay for usage (texts, calls, AI) on top of the monthly fee?
  • Who on your team works on Surge's account?
  • Can Surge get an export of all candidates, conversations and calendars at any time?
